title: Wrangler JK Unlimited
verdict: The Jeep that let Wrangler people have children, friends and luggage at the same time. The four-door JK turned a toy into a family car and an overland platform, and by 2017 three in four new Wranglers for sale were four-doors. Get the Pentastar, check the front end, and pack lighter than you think.

paragraphs: On April 12, 2006, at the New York Auto Show, Jeep did something it had resisted for 65 years: it put four doors on a Wrangler. The JK Unlimited kept everything that made a Wrangler a Wrangler (a separate frame, solid axles at both ends, a windshield that folds and doors that come off) and added 20.6 inches of wheelbase so adults could sit in the back. It was priced from $21,000. Purists predicted disaster. By mid-2017, three-quarters of the new Wranglers listed for sale were four-doors.

story.heading: LONGER THAN EVERYTHING BEFORE IT
paragraphs: Jeep had stretched its short-wheelbase rig before, with the [[jeep/cj-8|CJ-8 Scrambler]] and the TJ-based [[jeep/tj-unlimited|Wrangler Unlimited (LJ)]], but both added about 10 inches and kept two doors. The JK Unlimited added 20, for a 116-inch wheelbase against the two-door [[jeep/jk|JK]]'s 95.4, and yet it was only 14 inches longer overall than the 2006 LJ. It went on the line in August 2006 alongside the two-door at Toledo, Ohio, and it was the only four-door convertible on sale in America from the death of the Hummer H1 until the Ford Bronco arrived in July 2021.

Mechanically it is the same truck as the two-door. Driving Line's buyer's guide calls the two nearly identical and admits a soft spot for the Unlimited. X (later Sport), Sahara and Rubicon trims were offered from day one. Base trucks got a Dana 30 front axle, a Dana 44 rear and the Command-Trac transfer case with a 2.72:1 low range. The Rubicon added Dana 44s at both ends with electric Tru-Lok lockers, the 4:1 Rock-Trac transfer case and an electronically disconnecting front sway bar. Two-wheel-drive Unlimiteds were sold until 2010; from 2011, every one was a 4x4.

story.heading: 3.8 VERSUS 3.6
paragraphs: The JK's original engine was the minivan-derived 3.8-liter EGH V6, rated at 202 hp and 237 lb-ft, with a six-speed NSG370 manual or a four-speed 42RLE automatic. In a heavy four-door it was hard work, and Driving Line lists its habits: burning oil, intake-gasket failures, cracked exhaust manifolds, and a heat-stressed automatic once owners fitted bigger tires. The 2011 update gave the cabin a proper redesign, but the engine had to wait.

For 2012 the Pentastar 3.6 arrived with 285 hp and 260 lb-ft, plus a five-speed W5A580 automatic. Quadratec's spec history says it stopped being a 'rolling brick'. The Pentastar isn't flawless: some 2012–2013 Wrangler engines (2011–2013 across Chrysler's range) got a 10-year/150,000-mile warranty on the left cylinder head, and the plastic oil filter housing in the valley is a known leaker. It's still the JK engine to buy, and Driving Line recommends a 2013 or later truck for daily use.

story.heading: THE OVERLAND JEEP
paragraphs: The long wheelbase changed what a Wrangler was for. The four-door rode better, had a usable cargo area behind the rear seat and was rated to tow 3,500 lb against the two-door's 2,000. An industry grew up around it: roof racks, drawer systems, bumpers, and full conversions such as AEV's Brute, a 139-inch-wheelbase double-cab pickup inspired by the [[land-rover/defender-90-110|Defender 130]]. Mopar's own JK-8 Independence kit turned an Unlimited into a two-seat pickup in 2011.

The catch is weight. Payload is roughly 900 to 1,300 lb depending on year, trim and source, and a JKU with steel bumpers, a winch, a rooftop tent and two adults goes through that quickly. Expedition Portal's long-running payload thread is full of owners over their door-sticker rating. Their advice: spend on springs and shocks, and cut weight before you add more armor.

story.heading: HOW IT ENDED
paragraphs: Toledo built its millionth JK on May 17, 2013. The JK's last model year, 2018, overlapped the new [[jeep/jl-unlimited|JL Unlimited]], and fender decals told the two apart. Production ended on April 27, 2018, and the plant was retooled to build the JL-based Gladiator pickup. The JL kept the formula and fixed much of what JK owners complained about, but it didn't make the JKU obsolete. A well-sorted 2012–2018 Unlimited is still one of the cheapest ways into a solid-axle overland rig that will happily take 35s, and it is far easier to find parts for than a [[land-cruiser/80-series|Land Cruiser 80]].

callout.label: SIDEBAR · THE UNLIMITED GOES TO WORK
callout.title: Mail carriers, soldiers and the J8
paragraphs: Jeep built right-hand-drive Wranglers for US rural mail carriers, and for 2009 that job moved from the two-door to the right-hand-drive Unlimited.

In September 2007 Chrysler showed the J8, a military Unlimited with larger brakes, axles and suspension, heavy-duty rear leaf springs and a 2,952-lb (1,339 kg) payload. Power came from a 2.8-liter VM turbodiesel, and a hood-mounted snorkel allowed 30 inches of wading. It was to be built in Egypt and was never sold in the US, because it couldn't meet US emissions rules.

engineering_intro: The JK Unlimited is a body-on-frame four-door convertible with coil springs and solid axles front and rear, part-time four-wheel drive with a two-speed transfer case, and a 116-inch wheelbase. Unlike the TJ it replaced, it runs nearly everything except the steering through computer control, and it brought stability control to the Wrangler for the first time.

engineering.note: 20.6 in longer than the two-door JK's 95.4 in; about 185 in overall.
Driving Line rates the Dana 30 at about 35-in tires; on both axles the tubes and C-ends can bend.
Rubicon gets an electric Tru-Lok locker; Trac-Lok limited slip was optional on other trims. Quadratec says a few very early trucks had a Dana 35.
Both are versions of the NV241 part-time case; the 4:1 low range was Rubicon-only.
202 hp / 237 lb-ft, then 285 hp / 260 lb-ft. A 2.8 VM diesel was sold outside the US.
Plus 4.10 gears, 32-in BFGoodrich mud-terrains and rock rails.

generations_table.note: NSG370 6-speed manual or 42RLE 4-speed auto. 4x2 Unlimited offered until 2010; interior redesign for 2011.
NSG370 manual or W5A580 5-speed auto. Quadratec says the oil filter changed for 2014.
Dana 44 axles front and rear with Tru-Lok lockers, Rock-Trac 4:1, electronic sway-bar disconnect, 4.10 gears.
Upgraded 2.8 from 2011 with the five-speed W5A580. Not sold in the US.
Aftermarket 139-in-wheelbase double-cab pickup conversion of the Unlimited, retired after four years.
Sold alongside the new JL, with 'Wrangler JK' fender decals; production ended April 27, 2018.

buying_checks.head: Pick your engine first
buying_checks.body: 2007–2011 trucks have the 3.8 and four-speed automatic; 2012–2018 have the Pentastar and five-speed. Driving Line suggests 2013 or later for a daily driver and says any year is fine for a weekend trail rig.

buying_checks.head: Drive it over a pothole at 50 mph
buying_checks.body: Death wobble usually shows up at 45–65 mph after a bump. Have someone turn the wheel a quarter turn each way with the engine running while you watch both ends of the front track bar. Any movement at the bushing or bracket is a red flag.

buying_checks.head: Look at the oil filter housing
buying_checks.body: On a 3.6, pull the engine cover and look for oil in the valley at the back of the engine, and for oil on the bellhousing. The plastic housing is a known leaker. Curbside Classic's 2015 JK started leaking at about 55,000 miles.

buying_checks.head: On a 3.8, check for oil burning and manifold ticks
buying_checks.body: Ask how much oil it uses between changes, and listen for a cold-start exhaust tick, which can mean a cracked manifold. Driving Line also lists intake-gasket failures and, on hard-used engines, ring and main-bearing failures from about 100,000 miles.

buying_checks.head: 2012–2013: ask about the left cylinder head
buying_checks.body: Chrysler extended the warranty on the left cylinder head of affected 2012–2013 Wrangler Pentastars (2011–2013 across its range) to 10 years or 150,000 miles; its bulletin covers excessive cylinder leakage showing up as misfire codes. Ask whether the head has been replaced and get the dealer record.

buying_checks.head: Sight down the front axle
buying_checks.body: On lifted trucks with big tires, look for bent axle tubes or C-ends and uneven tire wear. Check for a truss. A bent Dana 30 housing usually means replacing it, often with a Dynatrac or Currie unit.

buying_checks.head: Weigh the build against the door sticker
buying_checks.body: Bumpers, a winch, a rack and a tent can put a JKU over its payload before anyone gets in. Check the sticker, and look at the rear coils and the bump-stop gap for sag.

buying_checks.head: Modified Jeeps: price the parts, then get a shop inspection
buying_checks.body: Driving Line's advice is to research every listed aftermarket part, have a 4x4 shop inspect the truck, and assume a heavily built Jeep has had a hard life.

repairs.title: Chase down death wobble (track bar first)
repairs.time: ≈ 1–3 hours to diagnose; longer if parts need replacing
repairs.cost: From free (re-torquing) to about $250–$400 for a JK track bar, per ExtremeTerrain's price guide
repairs.symptoms: Violent side-to-side shaking of the steering wheel and front axle, usually at 45–65 mph after a bump or bridge seam, which stops only when you slow right down.
repairs.fix: Check the front track bar first: with the engine running, have a helper turn the wheel a quarter turn each way while you watch both ends. If the bar moves without the bolt, or one end moves and the other doesn't, the bushing or bracket is worn. ExtremeTerrain lists the frame-side bolt at 125 ft-lb. Then work through the ball joints, tie-rod and drag-link ends, control-arm bushings and wheel bearings, and check tire balance and pressure. Replace whatever is loose, re-torque everything with the Jeep on the ground, and get an alignment. Quadratec and ExtremeTerrain both warn that a new steering stabilizer only hides the cause.
repairs.tools: Helper · torque wrench · large sockets · pry bar · floor jack and stands · paint pen to mark bolts.

parts.name: Crown Automotive front track bar 52059982AD, 2007–2018 JK

repairs.title: Replace the Pentastar oil filter housing / cooler (2012–2018)
repairs.time: ≈ 6 hours the first time (one owner's log)
repairs.cost: Housing plus gaskets and an oil change; tools under $30 for one owner
repairs.symptoms: Oil pooling in the valley under the intake, running over the back of the engine and dripping from the bellhousing. Sometimes coolant leaks too.
repairs.fix: Remove the engine cover and intake duct, then disconnect the injectors, coils, vacuum lines and brackets. Take off the upper intake (seven 8 mm bolts) and the lower manifold (eight bolts). Unplug the two sensors on the cooler and remove its five E8 external-Torx bolts. Mop the oil out of the valley, move the sensors and fittings to the new aluminum housing, fit new gaskets and O-rings, and torque in sequence. Reassemble, then refill the oil and coolant. Plug the intake ports with towels while you work. Don't overtighten the filter cap, which is specified at 18 lb-ft. Curbside Classic suspects overtightening contributes to the cracking.
repairs.tools: E8 external-Torx socket · 27 mm and 19 mm deep sockets · inch-pound torque wrench · hose clamp pliers · trim tool · shop vac · Dorman 926-876 aluminum housing (as used by Curbside Classic).

parts.name: Crown 68105583AF oil filter and cooler assembly, 2014–2016 JK 3.6
Crown 5184294RK oil filter adapter repair kit, 2012–2013 JK 3.6
Mopar/Dorman 68755454AA aluminum oil filter housing with element (check fitment)

repairs.title: Replace a cracked 3.8 exhaust manifold (2007–2011)
repairs.time: ≈ Half a day per side, more if studs break
repairs.cost: Manifold plus gaskets and studs; studs that snap add drilling time
repairs.symptoms: A ticking or puffing noise at cold start that quietens as the engine warms, a smell of exhaust in the engine bay, and soot marks at the manifold-to-head joint.
repairs.fix: Driving Line names cracked exhaust manifolds as a 3.8 weak point. Soak the studs in penetrating oil the night before. Unbolt the heat shield and the downpipe flange, then remove the manifold nuts. Inspect the studs and replace any that are stretched or corroded. Clean the head flange, fit new gaskets and a new manifold, and torque the nuts evenly from the center out. Check the oxygen sensor connectors and the downpipe gasket while you're in there.
repairs.tools: Penetrating oil · long extensions and swivels · stud extractor · torque wrench · new manifold studs and nuts.

repairs.title: Press in new front ball joints
repairs.cost: About $40–$60 a pair for stock joints, $200–$250 for a heavy-duty set of four (ExtremeTerrain)
repairs.symptoms: Clunks over bumps, wandering, uneven tire wear, or play when you rock a lifted wheel top to bottom. Worn joints can contribute to death wobble.
repairs.fix: Lift and support the axle, then remove the wheel, caliper, rotor, ABS sensor and the hub/bearing. Pull the axle shaft, then separate and remove the knuckle. Press out the upper and lower joints with a ball-joint press and the correct adapters, and press in the new ones square. Refit everything, torque to the factory figures (Northridge4x4 lists 75 ft-lb for the ball-joint nuts, 75 ft-lb for the hub bolts and 100 ft-lb for the axle nut), and get an alignment. Many owners replace the hub bearings and axle-shaft U-joints at the same time.
repairs.tools: Ball-joint press and JK adapter set · axle-nut socket · breaker bar · torque wrench · pickle fork or hammer for the tapers.

parts.name: Yukon YSPBJ-001HDK2 ball joint kit, JK Dana 30/44
OMIX 18036.05 genuine Dana Spicer ball joint kit, 2007–2018 JK
DV8 Offroad D-JKBLJNT-01 four-piece ball joint kit, JK Dana 30/44
JK tie rods, ends and ball joints

repairs.title: Replace a front hub and bearing
repairs.symptoms: A growl that changes with speed or while turning, play when you rock the wheel at 12 and 6 o'clock, or an ABS light from a damaged sensor.
repairs.fix: Lift the corner and remove the wheel, caliper bracket and rotor. Unplug the ABS sensor, remove the axle nut and the three hub bolts from the back of the knuckle, and pull the hub (it may need persuading). Clean the knuckle face, fit the new hub, and torque the bolts and axle nut (Northridge4x4: 75 ft-lb hub bolts, 100 ft-lb axle nut). Mopar lists different hubs for 2007–2010 and 2011–2018 JKs, so order by year.
repairs.tools: Large axle-nut socket · breaker bar · torque wrench · wire brush · anti-seize for the hub-to-knuckle face.

parts.name: OMIX 16705.14 front hub and bearing assembly, 2007–2018 JK

repairs.title: Truss a front axle before it bends (or after)
repairs.cost: Truss kit plus welding; a bent housing needs replacing, not trussing
repairs.symptoms: Toe that won't stay in alignment, inside-edge tire wear, or a visibly bent tube after a hard hit. It's common on lifted trucks running 35s and up on the factory axle.
repairs.fix: Driving Line says the small tubes and C-ends on both the Dana 30 and the Rubicon's Dana 44 can bend with oversized tires, and points to EVO Manufacturing trusses as a preventive fix. Check the housing is straight first, because a truss locks in whatever shape it has. Strip the axle (or at least remove the brackets that are in the way), grind the tubes clean, tack the truss in place, then weld in short alternating stitches to limit heat distortion. Paint it and re-check the alignment. If the housing is already bent, Dynatrac and Currie sell replacement housings.
repairs.tools: MIG or stick welder · grinder · straightedge or axle-alignment check · paint.

parts.name: JCR Offroad JKF-TRUSS-D30 front Dana 30 axle truss, JK
JCR Offroad JKF-TRUSS-44 front Dana 44 axle truss, JK
Rough Country 10565 Dana 30 truss and gusset kit, JK

repairs.title: Re-spring the rear for an overland load
repairs.cost: A pair of rear coils plus shocks; more if you go to a full lift
repairs.symptoms: A rear end that sags below the front, bottoms out on washboard, or sits on the bump stops with a full load of water, fuel and gear.
repairs.fix: Weigh the loaded truck first. Expedition Portal owners say the rear axle and suspension are the weak points under long-term heavy loads, and recommend springs and shocks rather than frame or axle changes. Support the frame, lower the axle on a jack after disconnecting the rear shocks, sway-bar links and track bar if needed, then swap the coils and fit the matching jounce bumpers. Refit at ride height and torque the suspension bolts with the Jeep on its wheels.
repairs.tools: Floor jack and frame stands · sockets · torque wrench · spring compressor not usually needed on JK rear coils.

parts.name: Skyjacker dual-rate rear coil spring pair, 2007–2018 JK Unlimited
OMIX 18280.26 rear coil spring jounce bumper, 2007–2018 JK

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: 33s. JK-Forum owners agree that most 285/70R17s (about 33 inches) fit on stock wheels, at stock height, with the stock bump stops. Expect light rubbing at full lock and at full flex, where they touch the flares, liners and sometimes the front sway bar. A steering-stop washer and the right backspacing help. ExtremeTerrain says 35s need at least a 2–3-inch lift, the right wheel offset and possibly new gears.

The 3.6 Pentastar (2012–2018) by a mile: 285 hp against 202, plus a five-speed automatic instead of the four-speed. The 3.8 is known for burning oil, intake-gasket leaks and cracked exhaust manifolds. Driving Line suggests a 2013 or later truck for daily use. A cheap 3.8 can still make a good trail rig if you accept its limits.

faq.q: How much can a JK Unlimited tow?
faq.a: 3,500 lb, with a 350-lb tongue weight for the 2017 Rubicon. That's against 2,000 lb for the two-door. For heavy towing the factory manual calls for synthetic 75W-140 in the rear axle.

Less than you think. Quadratec lists 1,067–1,301 lb for 2012 four-doors depending on trim. For 2017, KBB lists 880–1,000 lb and Cars.com gives the Rubicon 1,178 lb against a 5,700-lb GVWR. Your door-jamb sticker is the number that counts, and a fully built overland JKU often exceeds it.

faq.q: What fuel economy should I expect?
faq.a: The EPA rated the 2017 Unlimited 3.6 at 16 mpg city and 20 highway with the automatic (16/21 manual), and KBB lists a 22.5-gallon tank. Bigger tires, a lift and a rack all bring that down.

3.6 Pentastar: six quarts of 5W-20 meeting Chrysler MS-6395, or 5W-30 in hot climates. The filter is a cartridge under a cap on top of the engine, and Quadratec notes the filter changed for 2014, so buy for your year. The 3.8 also takes about six quarts with the filter, in 5W-20 or 5W-30; check the oil filler cap.

Every Rubicon has electric Tru-Lok lockers front and rear. Per Wikipedia, a rear locker was optional on X and Sahara for 2007, then only on select X models for 2008–2009; later the only non-Rubicon options were the 2015 Wrangler X and the 2016 75th Anniversary Edition. A Trac-Lok limited slip was the usual non-Rubicon option.

faq.q: Will the Dana 30 front axle handle 35s?
faq.a: Driving Line rates the non-Rubicon Dana 30 at about 35-inch tires. The tubes and C-ends can bend with big tires or hard use, and that's true of the Rubicon's Dana 44 too. Trusses help prevent it; replacement housings from Dynatrac or Currie are the cure.

faq.q: What do I do if it gets death wobble?
faq.a: Grip the wheel, don't brake hard, and slow down smoothly until it stops. Then fix the cause: start with the track bar, then the tie-rod ends, drag link, ball joints, control-arm bushings and wheel bearings, and check tire balance. A new steering stabilizer only masks it, and an alignment comes last.

In June 2014 Chrysler extended the warranty on the left cylinder head of some 2011–2013 3.6 V6s (2012–2013 on the Wrangler) to 10 years or 150,000 miles after cylinder-leakage misfires. Dealers replaced the head where testing showed excessive leakage, and AutoGuide reported that redesigned heads went into production in 2012. The extension has now run out, so a 2012–2013 truck with a misfire on that bank deserves a careful look.

faq.q: Is the four-door worse off-road than the two-door?
faq.a: On tight, technical trails the 116-inch wheelbase gives up breakover angle and turning circle compared with the 95.4-inch two-door. Everywhere else it rides better and carries more. Driving Line says the two are mechanically nearly identical and recommends driving both before you choose.

mods.why: 2.5–3.5 inches with matched coils and shocks clears 35s and can be specced for a loaded overland truck. Correct the track-bar and control-arm geometry, or death wobble will remind you.
Heavier tie rods, drag links and adjustable track bars keep big tires pointed where you want them and keep the front end tight.

mods.why: The long wheelbase makes the rockers the first thing to hit on a ledge.

who.name: DV8 Offroad SRSOTB-06 rock slider steps, JK Unlimited (Quadratec)

mods.why: The four-door roof is long enough for a proper platform, so you can keep weight off the tailgate. Mind the payload.

mods.why: The stock intake draws from the fender. A snorkel lifts it above the dust and spray.
A winch-ready steel front bumper is the usual first armor buy. Count its weight against the payload.

baseline_service.intro: With no receipts, assume nothing has been done. Change every fluid, and know which engine you have: the 3.8 (2007–2011) and the Pentastar (2012–2018) use different filters, plugs and automatic transmissions. Check the Pentastar's oil filter housing for leaks at the first oil change. Then do the gear oil, which is the service owners skip most. Rubicons and trucks with Trac-Lok need the right axle oil, and a limited-slip axle needs friction modifier.

items.spec: 3.6: 6 qt SAE 5W-20 meeting MS-6395 (5W-30 permitted) · 3.8: 6.0 qt with filter, 5W-20 or 5W-30 per the filler cap
items.interval: Then per the oil-life monitor or owner's manual [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: The Pentastar uses a cartridge filter under a 24 mm cap on top of the engine. Quadratec notes the filter changed for 2014, so buy for your year, and says to pull the old element gently because the pressure-relief valve is in the cap. Don't overtighten the cap; Curbside Classic gives 18 lb-ft.

items.interval: Inspect at every oil change; more often on dusty trails
items.note: If a snorkel or aftermarket intake is fitted, check the clamps and seals as well as the element.

items.note: Pentastar plugs are under the intake plenum on the rear bank, so it's a good time to look for oil filter housing seepage. 3.8 plugs: [CONFIRM IN MANUAL].

items.spec: 3.8 and 2012 3.6: HOAT 5-year/100,000-mile, about 13 qt · 2013–18 3.6: Mopar 10-year/150,000-mile OAT (MS.90032), 10.5 qt (ExtremeTerrain)
items.interval: KBB's schedule lists coolant at 100,000 mi; inspect hoses at every service
items.note: Don't mix HOAT and OAT; check what's in the tank before topping up. On a 3.6, a coolant leak in the valley can come from the oil cooler, not the water pump.

items.spec: W5A580 (2012–18): Mopar ATF+4, 5.3 qt service fill / 8.1 qt overhaul · 42RLE (2007–11): ATF+4, about 4.0 qt drain-and-fill / 8.8 qt total
items.interval: KBB lists transmission fluid at 100,000 mi; sooner if you tow or run big tires
items.note: Driving Line says heat kills both automatics, especially with oversized tires, towing or hard off-road use, and recommends an auxiliary cooler and proper gearing. A drain-and-fill with a new filter is the usual DIY.

items.spec: Mopar manual transmission lubricant meeting MS-9224 · 1.6 qt
items.interval: Change on a truck with unknown history [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: Driving Line says the NSG370 can grind, pop out of gear and get noisy, and recommends regular fresh fluid. A 2007 lube chart gives 22 ft-lb for the fill and drain plugs.

items.interval: Change on purchase, then per the severe-service schedule [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.note: Remove the fill plug before the drain plug. Both are chain-driven cases with aluminum housings (Driving Line), so don't overtighten the plugs.

items.interval: Change on purchase and after deep water crossings
items.note: If the oil looks milky, water has got in through the axle vent or seals.
